steps_walked.title: Keywords in your own language: the "translated from…" tags, "several senses", loading translation rings from Wikidata, and the keyword clean-up (fold)
prerequisites: A THROWAWAY data folder with the synthetic multilingual corpus, seeded with lemmatisation OFF so the fold has older word forms to fold. Seed first with no server running; the seed writes straight into the database file. From your Open-Omniscience folder run: (1) OO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/oo-rowM" OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 OO_EXTRACT_LEMMA=0 .venv/bin/python scripts/ui_clickthrough_seed.py  (2) OO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/oo-rowM" OO_DB_PLAINTEXT=1 .venv/bin/python -m uvicorn src.api.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8010  then open http://127.0.0.1:8010. Do NOT set OO_EXTRACT_LEMMA or OO_NO_SCHEDULER on the second command. The app must boot normally: lemmatisation on, and airplane mode on (the plane icon in the top bar is filled). Plaintext is fine because this row is not about encryption. If a first-launch language or terms screen appears, accept it and decline any offer to go online. To throw everything away afterwards, stop the server and delete $HOME/oo-rowM.
On the throwaway, do NOT press Settings → Advanced → Diagnostics → "Clean up keywords (re-index, then prune)" before M1. It re-indexes with lemmatisation on and leaves nothing for the fold to fold.

Your REAL encrypted install, unlocked, on its usual address. You need it for M3 parts (3)–(4) (the synthetic corpus has almost no acronyms, so the entity lists are empty there), for M6 if the throwaway has no multi-meaning word, for M7 if the throwaway shows no "rising" Lead card, and for M10–M11.

A FRESH BACKUP of the real install before M11 (and ideally before M10): Settings → Data & backup → Export / Backup panel → "Export / Back up…" (#set-data). Or stop the app and copy the whole data folder (USER_MANUAL §5.1). A fold cannot be undone without a backup.
Optional, for M5(c): your local AI (Ollama with a model installed) running on this machine. The app reaches a local Ollama over loopback even in airplane mode, so this does NOT require going online.

A browser window at least 1280 px wide (the sandbox measured at 1280×900), and a way to record: for each step id, write pass or fail plus a screenshot per surface and per language. The session files these under docs/audit/ as the Q1128 = a record.

Rule for the whole walk: never click the small red ✕ beside a keyword (in Insights lists and on the Trends bar rows). It hides that keyword everywhere. If you click one by mistake: Settings → Advanced → "Keywords — explore, curate, filter" → Keyword filtering → delete the word from "Excluded keywords (yours)" → press "Save keyword filter".

steps.do: (a) Click "Fold report (.json)" BEFORE any fold and look at the browser tab it opens, then close that tab. (b) Click "Fold keyword forms (studies → study)", read the confirmation, and press OK. (c) Watch the grey status line until it stops changing (it refreshes every 2 seconds).
steps.expect: (a) The new tab shows only a short error answer containing "no-report". No report, whether invented or all zeros, appears before a fold has finished. (b) The confirmation says older keywords are filed under the base form, so “studies” and “study” become one keyword; that phrases, names and keywords your families or groups use are left as they are; that it runs in the background and can be paused from the task manager. It ends with "A fold cannot be undone." (c) On this small corpus the line may jump straight to the end. If you catch it mid-run, it reads "Keywords checked: X of Y (Z%)" (possibly followed by "· Mentions moved: N") and then "Setting each keyword's language from its mentions…". The final line reads "Keywords folded: N · mentions moved: M · keywords whose language changed: K" with N and M above 0, because this folder was seeded with lemmatisation off. There is no raw error text. If the line instead says "Lemmatisation is off in this install (OO_EXTRACT_LEMMA=0)…", the server was started with that variable: restart it without the variable. That is a setup error, not a fail.

steps.expect: The report now opens. It contains a "fold" block of counts (keywords_folded, mentions_moved, mentions_merged, skipped_phrase, unchanged…). It contains a "largest_folds" list of entries shaped {"from", "to", "lang", "mentions"}. In each entry, "to" is the base form of the SAME word in that "lang" (e.g. from "districts" to "district" with "lang": "en"); no entry merges two different words or turns a word into another language's word. It contains "curated_left_unfolded_sample" (may be empty). It contains a "language" block, which is the reconcile pass (Q413/Q414), with relanguaged, votes_from_mentions, votes_from_articles and "complete": true. It contains a "lemmatiser" block whose "languages" are exactly de, en, es, fr, id, it, nl, pt, ru (no zh, ja or ar), and a plain-language "method". The second fold finishes with "Keywords folded: 0 · mentions moved: 0 · keywords whose language changed: …" (normally 0), which shows it is safe to re-run.

steps.expect: The status line shows "Loading in the background…". In the task manager, under "AI & analysis", a "running" row reads "Loading keyword translations from Wikidata" (in English in every UI language). It has a bar "i / 5 · P%" and, under it, the keyword being looked up: the word itself, never a web address. The bar never reaches 5/5, because it counts keywords started and the row vanishes when the job ends. R8 allows at most one request per 10 seconds: each keyword takes at least 10 s, or at least 20 s when Wikidata finds a match, so 5 keywords can never finish in under about 40 s and usually take 1.5–2 minutes. A faster run breaks R8. At the end the status reads "Rings loaded: W/5" (W from 0 to 5; "stopped early" only if it was stopped). Its hover shows the method ("…spaced at one per 10 seconds…") and the caveat word for word. Report as a contradiction: that caveat ends "Edit or delete the file to undo a load.", while the panel says "do not delete the whole of it". The "no ring" number has dropped, usually by at least W. Also record whether the task manager offers a Cancel button for this job: the server marks it cancellable, but no code draws a button for this job kind. The plane is empty (online) during the load and filled again after you click it.

verdicts.title: After a fold, keyword surfaces show the old inflected term, and clicking or hovering it resolves to the emptied pre-fold keyword (0 mentions)
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on my own encrypted seed (OO_EXTRACT_LEMMA=0 at seed time only, port 8828). I ran the fold from Diagnostics, then clicked the landscape chip 'nouvelle in French'. It gave 'Resolved to nouvelle term · 0 mentions in 0 articles', while typing 'nouveau' gave 109 mentions in 55 articles (Mr-D1-landscape-click-nouvelle-en.png, r2.json). The API shows the same thing: /api/insights/top returns {term:'nouvelle', normalized:'nouveau', mentions:109}; trend?term=nouvelle returns 0; registros→0 and registro→83; keyword-stats?term=районах returns 0 mentions, while район returns 55. The emptied rows really remain in the DB ('errors' and 'errores' at mention_count 0). They persist indefinitely on an offline install, because the prune runs only in the scheduler's idle window (src/scheduler/maintenance.py), and the scheduler does not start in airplane mode.
verdicts.root_cause: src/analytics/queries.py:220-225 resolve_keyword returns the first exact normalized_term match before it tries _resolve_by_lemma, even when that row has zero mentions. The fold (src/analytics/keyword_fold.py:273-277) creates or keeps the target with term=src.term, the inflected surface, and deliberately leaves the emptied source row for prune_orphan_keywords (OPEN_QUEUE 'LEFT OUT: deleting the keywords a fold empties'). Every click and hover passes the display term (app-insights.js:142 pickTerm(f.term); app-corpus.js:1156 data-kwstat=term.term; termListHtml 1231), so it lands on the orphan.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In resolve_keyword, when the exact normalized hit has mention_count == 0, fall through to _resolve_by_lemma and return that row when it finds one, keeping the orphan only as a last resort. The alternative is to have the fold call prune_orphan_keywords on the rows it emptied as its final step. Either one keeps the fold equal to a re-index.

For example: const inner = e.target.closest('.oo-tip-target'); if (inner && inner !== el) { hovered = null; return; }. verdicts.title: Fold is not a fixed point, so a second run folds again, and one largest_fold merges two different words
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: the first fold ended 'Keywords folded: 350 · mentions moved: 7,552 · keywords whose language changed: 10'. The second run, from the same UI button, ended 'Keywords folded: 1 · mentions moved: 27 · keywords whose language changed: 0', with largest_folds [{from:'cooperativa', to:'cooperativo', lang:'pt', mentions:27}] and targets_created 1 (r1.json, fold_report_second.json). This contradicts OPEN_QUEUE's 'the fold is idempotent (a second run moves nothing, tested)' and the Q416 index note 'the lemma is pinned idempotent'. Measured with the app's own lemmatize: cooperativas→cooperativa→cooperativo and filas→fila→filar. The idempotence test (tests/test_keyword_lemma_extraction.py:122) only checks 'en'. Since lemma_key is shared, extraction of new articles files 'cooperativas' under 'cooperativa' while a later fold moves it to 'cooperativo', recreating the split the job exists to remove. The fila→filar entry (noun 'queue' filed under verb 'filar') is simplemma's dictionary, applied identically at extraction, so it is a lemma-quality issue rather than a fold bug. No mention is lost, hence P3.
verdicts.root_cause: src/analytics/extract.py:461-494. lemma_key adopts a lemma that is not itself a fixed point of extraction_lemma (src/analytics/lemma.py lemmatize), and keyword_fold.py's classify step (rules.movable(norm), ~keyword_fold.py:656) re-applies it to keys that are already lemmas.
verdicts.suggested_fix: In lemma_key, adopt lem only when extraction_lemma(lem, language) == lem, otherwise keep word, so one pass is always a fixed point for both callers. Extend test_lemmatisation_is_idempotent to every LEMMA_LANGS language. Add 'fila' to the evidence-grown MISLEMMA_DENYLIST.

verdicts.title: Language reconcile tags English words as Spanish in the English UI ('software in Spanish', 'errors in Spanish')
verdicts.reason: Half confirmed, half by design. 'software': the seed's English and Spanish specimen texts both use the word, and its mentions are en 18 / es 27. Q414 = a ('derive the keyword's language as the majority') makes it es, and the ladder tags it 'in Spanish'; that half is by design. 'errors' is a real defect. Before the fold, 'errors' (en) and 'errores' (es) were separate keywords. The fold keyed both to lemma 'error', one row with mentions en 18 / es 27, whose display term is the English surface 'errors' and whose language is es. So the UI shows the English word 'errors' labelled 'in Spanish', a false statement (DB read, walk en/fr: 'errors en espagnol 45'). Brief S04-06 S5 requires lemmatisation 'at EXTRACTION, never across languages (families.py:336)', where the display-time grouping keys (kind, lang, lemma).
verdicts.root_cause: src/analytics/extract.py:461-494 (lemma_key) keys a term by its lemma alone, and src/analytics/store.py:197-204 (_get_or_create_keyword) and keyword_fold.py:268-277 match targets on normalized_term only. Two languages' different words that share a lemma therefore merge into one row. The fold names the target with the first source's surface (term=src.term, keyword_fold.py:276), while reconcile_keyword_language sets the majority language.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Do not adopt a lemma (at extraction and in the fold) when it would merge surfaces from different languages into one key. The smallest check is in the fold: skip a target whose existing mentions are in another language. Otherwise record it for a ruling, since S5 forbids it. At the label, when a keyword's mention languages are split, name the split ('in Spanish and English', with counts in the hover) rather than a single language.

verdicts.title: A tag's hover lacks the ring's other members with per-language counts (Q401/Q418)
verdicts.reason: Reproduced (fr): the landscape 'logiciel' tag's bubble reads 'Traduction vérifiée (concept translangue). — Original: software — Langue: espagnol — Wikidata: Q7397', with no ring members or counts. The API row for 'software' (target_lang=en/fr) carries language_breakdown: None, while only merged ring rows such as 'transport' carry {fr:69, es:56, ar:28}. Q401 (a) requires 'the ring's other members with counts', and Q418 (a) requires 'ring members with per-language counts'.
verdicts.root_cause: src/analytics/queries.py:682-731. _annotate_translations adds only tier/source language/QID/senses to a solo verified row. src/static/app-corpus.js:880-893 kwHoverText adds kwLangBreakdownText only when row.language_breakdown exists, which it never does for these rows.
verdicts.suggested_fix: When the ladder resolves a solo row to a verified ring, attach that ring's members present in the corpus with their per-language mention counts (the same shape queries.trending already emits as language_breakdown), so kwHoverText's existing branch renders them.

verdicts.title: The 'local AI offline' toast tells the user to switch off airplane mode for a loopback Ollama
verdicts.reason: Reproduced (fr, no Ollama, airplane on): '✦ Traduire le reste' raised 'L'IA locale est hors ligne — démarrez Ollama (et désactivez le mode avion) pour des traductions provisoires.' (Mr-D13-ai-toast-fr.png). Loopback Ollama is explicitly allowed under the kill switch: src/llm/ollama.py:532-574 (_check_kill_switch refuses only a non-loopback base_url or a clearnet pull); the triage_job docstring confirms that loopback runs work in airplane mode, as does CLAUDE.md's airplane non-negotiable. The advice needlessly nudges the operator to go online.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-corpus.js:1215, the toast string (and its 12 locale entries). The stale docstring in src/api/ai.py:283-284 ('including airplane mode') repeats the same wrong premise.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Change the string to say only 'Local AI is offline — start Ollama for tentative translations.' ×12. Mention airplane mode only when OO_OLLAMA_URL is non-loopback, which the client already names in its own error. Correct the endpoint docstring.

verdicts.title: Untranslated English on keyword surfaces in fr/ar/zh
verdicts.reason: Re-observed in fr: 'Resolved to software term · 90 mentions in 72 articles' (explore line); the Analysis Combine hint '… set algebra over N keywords. The set expression is the corpus label; counts only, never a score.'; the keyword-stats bubble caveat 'Counts only, never a score. The trend ratio is noisy…'; Super-groups '· 7 members · 469 mentions Dominated by voting (78% of this total)'; the task-manager label 'Folding keyword forms into their base form'; and the fr grammar slip '2 mentions, contre 2 sur les période précédente' on Home Tendances actuelles. fr.json has no key at all for 'Resolved to', 'set algebra over', 'Folding keyword forms…', 'Single-source', 'spread across', 'Resurfaced after' or 'Through time'. The Home card titles are plain English f-strings (producers.py:1038, 2146, 2762); only the rising card has title_i18n (:298).
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-corpus.js:699 ('Resolved to' literal, not t()) and :1089 (Combine hint literal); caveats sent by the server and rendered with esc(d.caveat) without a locale key; src/static/taskmanager.html:312 and app-core.js:1893 print esc(j.label) from src/api/jobs.py:497-499 without t(); src/briefing/producers.py card titles lack title_i18n; the fr.json template '{n} mentions, contre {prior} sur les {window}' hard-codes the plural article before a {window} that can be singular ('période précédente').
verdicts.suggested_fix: Wrap the literals in t()/tf() with keys ×12. Key the job labels and card titles as templates (title_i18n + title_vars, as the rising card does). Reword the fr template to avoid the article (e.g. 'contre {prior} ({window})').
